newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai to make rules on foreign banks business.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai to make rules on foreign banks business.

text.p: Shanghai plans to promulgate detailed rules on foreign banks doing local Chinese yuan business before the end of March to allow the eight designated overseas banks to start business in the second quarter, the Shanghai Securities News said on Friday.
The decision was made at a recent meeting on foreign bank business in Shanghai organised by the Shanghai branch of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, the newspaper said.

Eight overseas banks have won approval to do local Chinese yuan business but a lack of detailed rules on operations and a precondition that they move to the Pudong district to the east of central Shanghai have delayed a start.

The banks are the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp, Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank, the Industrial Bank of Japan, Sanwa Bank of Japan, Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank of Japan, Standard Chartered Bank of Britain and the International Bank of Paris and Shanghai, a joint venture between France's Banque National de Paris and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.
"It has been decided that details of rules on foreign banks doing yuan business will be worked out in the first quarter of 1997," the newspaper said.
"This will allow those foreign banks that have won approval to start business in the second quarter," it said.
The newspaper said Citibank was the first among the eight to have moved to Pudong and that others had chosen their offices in Pudong and would move there soon.
By the end of 1996, Shanghai had a total of 46 foreign bank branches and 147 bank representative offices.
